mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (below 0.1%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces the cost of capital for equities, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 10.0 percentage points, it signals a severe labor market contraction that typically precedes a recession, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 10.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in employment growth (PAYEMS growth rate < 0.0%) and a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE > 10.0%) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS growth < 0.0% and UNRATE > 10.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a recession (defined by a quarterly decline in real GDP, GDPC1 < 0.0%), a rising housing starts index (HOUST > 1200.0) signals an early recovery in the housing sector, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when HOUST > 1200.0 and GDPC1 shows a quarterly decline, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO > 95.0) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as it signals improving economic activity.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO > 95.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI index level above 255.0 (indicating elevated price levels) signals persistent inflationary pressures that prompt central bank tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 255.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in retail sales (RSAFS growth rate > 0.5%) and housing starts (HOUST > 1200.0) indicates strong consumer and housing demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when RSAFS growth > 0.5% and HOUST > 1200.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a high unemployment regime (UNRATE > 10.0%), a positive employment growth rate (PAYEMS growth > 0.5%) signals a labor market recovery, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 10.0 and PAYEMS growth > 0.5%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
